chunks: Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a man who owes me money and repays me partly in dinars and partly in dirhams. Then when he comes to settle the account with me in full, the price of the dinars has changed. Which of the two prices should I calculate by: the price that was on the day he gave me the dinars, or the price of the day I settle the account with him?
He عليه السلام said: "The price of the day he gave you the dinars, because you withheld their benefit from him."

key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرَ: gold dinars used here as one form of payment in settling a debt
key_terms.حَبَسْتَ: you withheld or retained, referring to preventing the other party from benefit
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver dirhams used here alongside dinars in partial repayment
key_terms.سِعْرُ: the market rate or exchange value under discussion
key_terms.لِيُوَفِّيَنِي: to pay me in full or complete what is owed
key_terms.مَنْفَعَتَهَا: the benefit or utility of the money
key_terms.يُحَاسِبُنِي: to settle or calculate the account between creditor and debtor

ai.seo_question: When repaying a debt partly in dinars and partly in dirhams, which day's exchange rate should be used in the final settlement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about settling a debt paid in mixed currencies when exchange values change over time. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the calculation is based on the value on the day the dinars were given, establishing a principle tied to the benefit that had already been withheld from the debtor.
